ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
An ideal transformer has a primary coil with a number of turns $n_{1}$, and two secondary coils, I and II. All meters are ideal. It is known that the reading of the $V_{1}$ meter is $220\mathrm{V}$, the reading of the A meter is $0.5\mathrm{A}$, the number of turns of secondary coil I is $n_{2}=25$, the reading of the $V_{2}$ meter is $5\mathrm{V}$, and $R_{1}=5\Omega$.

1. Find the number of turns in the primary coil $n_{1}$.
2. What is the output power \( P_{2} \) of the secondary coil II?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: An ideal transformer has a primary coil with a number of turns $n_{1}$, and two secondary coils, I and II. All meters are ideal. It is known that the reading of the $V_{1}$ meter is $220\mathrm{V}$, the reading of the A meter is $0.5\mathrm{A}$, the number of turns of secondary coil I is $n_{2}=25$, the reading of the $V_{2}$ meter is $5\mathrm{V}$, and $R_{1}=5\Omega$. 1. Find the number of turns in the primary coil $n_{1}$. 2. What is the output power \( P_{2} \) of the secondary coil II?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is the primary-side circuit of an ideal transformer. The AC power supply is connected to the primary coil, and the primary coil is labeled n1; the A meter is connected in series in the primary circuit, and the V1 meter is connected in parallel across the two ends of the primary coil. On the right side there are two secondary coils: the upper secondary coil is labeled I, the number of turns is labeled n2, the V2 meter is connected in parallel across the two ends of this secondary coil, and the resistor R1 is also connected to the output end of the same secondary side I; the lower secondary coil is labeled II and separately supplies power to the resistor R2. Reasoning: It is known that V1=220 V, the reading of the A meter is the primary current I1=0.5 A, the number of turns of secondary side I is n2=25, V2=5 V, and R1=5 Ω. For an ideal transformer under the same magnetic flux, voltage is proportional to the number of turns, so n1/n2=V1/V2. Substituting gives n1=25×(220/5)=25×44=1100 turns. The primary input power is Pin=V1 I1=220×0.5=110 W. The ideal transformer and ideal meters do not consume power, so the total output power of the two secondary sides is equal to 110 W. The power of R1 in secondary side I is P_I=V2^2/R1=5^2/5=5 W. Therefore the output power of secondary side II is P2=110−5=105 W.
